wine_name: Terroir Al Limit Les Tosses, Catalunya
wrong_facts: Hook says vines are 110 years old; ground truth says 90-year-old vines
Hook says vineyard is in Poboleda; ground truth says it's in Torroja del Priorat
Hook claims 1,500 bottles per hectare yield — fabricated number not in context data
Hook claims 45-degree pitches — fabricated specific number
Wine summary says co-founded by Dominik Huber and Jaume Sabaté; ground truth says co-founded with Eben Sadie
Terroir section says 500-meter altitude; ground truth says 600m elevation
Vinification says 8 months in neutral French oak; ground truth says recent vintages ferment and age in cement tanks, no wood aging
Vinification mentions foot-treading — not in context data or ground truth
Vinification says 'short macerations'; ground truth says two weeks on skins
Value assessment fabricates $110-140 price range — no prices provided in context
fabricated_numbers: 8 months in neutral French oak (context says 8 months oak but ground truth says cement tanks)
reasoning: The hook contains two provably wrong facts (Poboleda instead of Torroja, 110-year-old instead of 90-year-old vines) which triggers the hard cap of 1.5 on correctness. Multiple fabricated numbers compound the problem: yield per hectare, slope angle, price range, and altitude are all invented. The co-founder is wrong (Jaume Sabaté instead of Eben Sadie). The vinification description claims neutral French oak when ground truth says cement tanks with no wood. Voice is strong — direct, opinionated, no banned words, good structure. Specificity is good in naming soils, producers, and dishes, but many specific claims are wrong. Usefulness is undermined by the factual errors despite good structural information.
